claims.text: An oscillating SLM scanning strategy followed by rapid solution annealing can enable fabrication of a Group IV–V refractory high-entropy alloy with improved structural performance.
The proposed processing route will retain a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The proposed processing route will produce and retain a high dislocation density.
The proposed processing route will suppress Laves-phase precipitation.
High cooling rates during SLM suppress equilibrium phase formation.
Annealing in an inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during post-processing.
Rapid solution annealing at a temperature below matrix melting can dissolve incipient Laves phases.
An oscillating scan strategy can manipulate crystallographic texture.
An oscillating scan strategy introduces a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations.
A high dislocation density acts as a barrier to crack propagation.
Rapid SLM cooling kinetically traps the refractory alloy in a metastable single-phase state.
Cr promotes formation of brittle Laves phases in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Silicides, B2 phases, and Laves phases are intrinsically brittle secondary phases associated with poor tensile ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Suppressing brittle secondary phases at grain boundaries mitigates brittle fracture.
Retained dislocations provide high-temperature strengthening without requiring brittle precipitates.
The proposed microstructure mitigates brittleness caused by interstitial oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon.
The processed alloy will have greater high-temperature strength and creep resistance than conventionally cast or slowly cooled counterparts.
The processed alloy will have greater oxidation resistance than conventionally cast or slowly cooled counterparts.
The processed alloy will exhibit enhanced ductility relative to conventionally cast, slowly cooled, or raster-scanned counterparts.
Cr-containing Group IV–V refractory alloys in which interstitial impurities are the primary source of brittleness define the applicable alloy space.

contradictions.description: The alloy family is labeled as Group IV–V, but the example feedstock includes Mo and W and the boundary requires Cr; those elements fall outside the stated Group IV–V scope.

The hypothesis predicts a single-phase BCC solid solution, whereas the mediator is phrased as a suppressed volume fraction of secondary phases, which permits a nonzero multiphase state. The intended final phase criterion is therefore ambiguous.
